title: From Approval to Abuse: Privilege Escalation Attacks on Harness-Protected Coding Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.22987v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Coding agents use execution harnesses to constrain the consequences of prompt injection by enforcing permission boundaries. These systems deterministically intercept any out-of-sandbox action and prompt the user for approval. To reduce approval fatigue, users can approve allow-rules proposed by the agent, after which any future action matching the rule is allowed without a prompt. In this work, we show that this mechanism introduces a new risk: untrusted context can influence the permissions presented for approval, with consequences extending beyond the immediate task. We investigate privilege escalation targeting this permission-update process. Specifically, adversarial context planted in a repository can reliably steer an agent performing a routine task into requesting a plausibly justified, yet dangerously broad allow-rule. translated_title: 从批准到滥用：针对受框架保护的编码代理的权限提升攻击
translated_abstract: 编码代理使用执行框架通过强制权限边界来限制提示注入的后果。这些系统会确定性地拦截任何沙箱外的操作，并提示用户进行批准。为了减少批准疲劳，用户可以批准代理提出的允许规则，此后任何匹配该规则的未来操作都将无需提示即可执行。在这项工作中，我们展示了这一机制引入了一种新的风险：不可信的上下文可以影响呈报给用户批准的权限，其后果超出了当前任务的范畴。我们研究了针对这一权限更新过程的权限提升攻击。具体而言，植入仓库中的对抗性上下文可以可靠地引导执行常规任务的代理请求一条看似合理但范围危险过宽的允许规则。如果用户批准了该请求，保存的规则实际上会使框架失效失明，使攻击者能够执行……
tldr: 本文揭示了编码代理权限批准机制中的新型权限提升攻击：仓库中植入的对抗性内容可诱导代理请求看似合理实则范围过宽的允许规则，一旦用户批准，攻击者便能利用该规则使安全框架失效并滥用代理权限。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals a novel privilege escalation attack on coding agents' permission approval mechanisms, showing that adversarial content planted in a repository can reliably steer agents into requesting plausibly justified yet dangerously broad allow-rules, which once approved can blind the harness and enable abuse by adversaries.
